cues.en: Hi. So we have a little bit of business before we get started. I'm supposed to ask you to pretty please mute your cell phones so they don't go off. And also to make sure to fill out your surveys when you're done or when we're done. They're super helpful for GDC to figure out who they should invite back. And they're also super useful for me to figure out if you liked the way I presented and you like what I presented. So please take a moment when we're done to do that. All right. That's the stuff out of the way. Let's get started.
cues.zh: 大家好。在开始之前先交代几件小事。我得拜托大家务必把手机静音，以免响起来打扰大家。另外，结束后请务必填写调查问卷。这对 GDC 决定之后邀请谁回来演讲非常有帮助。对我来说也很有用，能让我知道大家喜不喜欢我的演讲风格和分享的内容。所以结束后请花点时间填一下。好的，事项交代完毕，我们马上开始。

cues.en: So my name is John McDonald. I'm here from Valve and today I wanted to come and talk a little bit about how we've been using deep learning to effectively combat cheating in CSGO. Spoiler alert, it works pretty well. We're pretty happy with it. So that's a bunch of stuff. We have a whole hour, so we're going to cover a lot of ground.
cues.zh: 我叫 John McDonald，来自 Valve。今天我想来聊聊我们如何利用深度学习，有效打击 CSGO 中的作弊行为。先剧透一下：效果非常好，我们相当满意。内容挺多的，我们有一整小时，所以会讲到很多方面。

cues.en: I'm going to spend a little bit of time, fair warning, probably about 15 minutes kind of talking about the state of CSGO with respect to cheating other things that we do in this space. And then we'll dive into sort of the pitch that I was making to folks around Valve in 2016 for why we should maybe give this a try. We'll dive into results. And then we'll talk a little bit about how you train and utilize deep networks. We'll talk about some ongoing and near-term work, and then we'll finish up.
cues.zh: 先提醒一下，我会先花大概 15 分钟，聊聊 CSGO 目前的反作弊现状，以及我们在这个领域所做的其他工作。接着会讲讲 2016 年我在 Valve 内部向大家推销这个想法时的提案——为什么我们应该试一试。然后看实际成果。之后会谈谈如何训练和使用深度神经网络。再聊聊目前正在进行和近期的工作，最后做个总结。

cues.en: One thing that's probably worth mentioning is that notably absent from this list is deep learning. I'm not actually going to try and teach you deep learning in an hour because I don't believe that I can do it. But I will point you at the end towards resources so that if, when we're done, you feel like, oh, that's something that maybe I should try, you know where to get started. And good news, it's actually pretty straightforward to learn. All right, so let's talk a little bit about CSGO itself first.
cues.zh: 有一点值得提一下，这个大纲里明显没有“深度学习基础”。我确实没打算在一小时内教会大家深度学习，因为我觉得自己做不到。但我会在最后推荐一些资源，要是听完后觉得“这套路我也想试试”，你就知道从哪儿上手了。好消息是，它学起来其实相当简单直接。好，那我们先来聊聊 CSGO 本身。

cues.en: CSGO, if you're unfamiliar, I think most of you probably are, but it is a succession of Counter Strike. It is a competitive multiplayer game. It's fast-paced action. We have sort of bullets that are extremely, extremely lethal. And when you're dead for a round, you're out. The combat engagements in CSGO are very, very short. The average engagement time can be like one to two seconds. And all of this sort of matters because it impacts our cheating problem.
cues.zh: 如果大家对 CSGO 不太熟悉——不过我想大部分人都知道——它是 Counter Strike 的正统续作。这是一款多人竞技动作游戏，节奏非常快。游戏中的子弹杀伤力极强，单局阵亡后就只能等下一轮。CSGO 的交火接触时间非常非常短，平均交火时间大概只有一两秒。而所有这些特性都很关键，因为它们直接影响了作弊问题的性质。

cues.en: CSGO has 12.4 million monthly uniques and 3 million uniques checked back in every day, so we're pretty happy that our player base is so rabid. Finally, it's the 10th title that shipped on Source Engine, and we'll see how this plays into our cheating problem a little bit later as well.
cues.zh: CSGO 拥有 1240 万月活跃独立用户，每天有 300 万独立用户上线，看到玩家群体如此狂热，我们非常欣慰。最后，它是基于 Source 引擎发布的第十款作品，稍后我们也会看到这一点是如何与作弊问题交织在一起的。

cues.en: One of our most popular modes for CSGO is the competitive mode. It's a 5v5 game mode. First to 16 wins, and each round is about two minutes and 57 seconds. When you sign in for matchmaking, we ask you to agree that you could be signing up for a 90-minute commitment. The average game is actually more like 40 minutes. 65% of our players check back in with this mode at least once a month.
cues.zh: 我们最受欢迎的 CSGO 模式之一就是竞技模式。它是 5v5 模式，先赢 16 回合获胜，每回合大约 2 分 57 秒。你排队匹配时，我们会让你同意，这可能意味着你要投入 90 分钟。平均一局其实更像 40 分钟。65% 的玩家每月至少会回来玩一次这个模式。

cues.en: And there are 600,000 of these matches every day. It varies depending on time of day and, sorry, day of week and summer. There's a lot more matches, school's out, et cetera. But it turns out college kids love to play video games. I don't know if any of y'all knew that. So let's dive in and talk about cheating, because that's kind of why we're here.
cues.zh: 每天有 60 万场这种对局。具体数量会随时段变化，抱歉，是随星期几和暑期变化。学校放假等等，对局会多很多。结果大学生超爱打电子游戏。不知道在座各位有没有人知道。那我们深入聊聊作弊吧，因为这正是我们在这里的原因。

cues.en: Back in 2016, I was sort of figuring out what I was going to work on next. I had finished up some other CSGO work, and I was trying to figure out what I wanted to do. And usually when I'm in that space of Valve, I just kind of try and sort of figure out what the community wants, because I figure any time you sort of pay down some debt in the community, that's a pretty good investment while you're trying to figure out sort of larger problem to work on. And it turns out I couldn't do that, because the only thing the community was talking about was cheating.
cues.zh: 2016 年，我在琢磨接下来要做什么。我完成了其他一些 CSGO 工作，想确定自己想做点什么。通常当我在 Valve 的那种空档期，我会试着搞清楚社区想要什么，因为我觉得，每当你在社区偿还一些欠账，在你还想解决更大问题的时候，这就是很好的投资。结果我做不到，因为社区唯一在谈的就是作弊。

cues.en: It was this just deafening conversation, and we saw this. And of course, this information is all anecdotal, but we saw it on Reddit, and we saw it on our own CSGO team feedback alias, where players mail us directly. And the feedback alias, in particular, I had some data on. It was like 90% of the incoming mail was people saying, your game is filled with cheaters. And that's really frustrating. But we weren't sure whether or not the problem was
cues.zh: 那是一场震耳欲聋的讨论，我们看到了。当然这些信息都是传闻，但我们在 Reddit 上看到，也在我们自己的 CSGO 团队反馈邮箱里看到，玩家直接给我们发邮件。尤其是反馈邮箱，我有一些数据。大约 90% 的来信都是说，你们游戏全是作弊者。这真的让人沮丧。但我们不确定问题究竟是

cues.en: sort of a perception problem or whether there was actually a cheating problem, except it turned out that vac bans, which we'll talk about in a little bit, sort of supported this conversation. Like we had a lot of vac bans that we were handing out.
cues.zh: 一种认知问题，还是确实存在作弊问题；结果发现，VAC 封禁——我们稍后会讲到——某种程度上印证了这种讨论。我们当时发出了很多 VAC 封禁。

cues.en: And we think that CSGO has sort of two main components that lead to cheating being such a significant problem. And there's a third aspect we'll talk about in a little bit. But one is that the design is this very satisfying combat experience where almost any weapon in the game can be a one-shot kill. But that does also sort of fail to disincentivize cheating.
cues.zh: 我们认为 CSGO 有两个主要因素，导致作弊成为如此严重的问题。还有第三个方面，我们稍后会谈。其一是，设计上是非常爽快的战斗体验，游戏里几乎任何武器都能一枪毙命。但这也确实没能抑制作弊。

cues.en: On balance, we think that's a good trade because players really enjoy this, but it does sort of make us a juicy target for cheating. Similarly, since the engine is so old, and about 75 to 80% of the code in CSGO is actually unchanged from Half-Life 2, that means that if you have a cheat that somebody wrote back in, say, 2005 for Half-Life 2 deathmatch, and then they posted it on GitHub a couple of years ago on a lark,
cues.zh: 权衡之下，我们认为这是值得的取舍，因为玩家真的很喜欢，但这确实让我们成了作弊的诱人目标。同样，由于引擎太老，CSGO 约 75% 到 80% 的代码实际上和 Half-Life 2 相比没有改动，这意味着如果有人写了一个作弊程序，比如 2005 年为 Half-Life 2 死亡竞赛写的，然后几年前一时兴起发到 GitHub 上，

cues.en: I think probably actually works on CSGO with a small amount of changes, like maybe five to 10 minutes of tinkering. Now, the good news is we do actually catch pretty much all of those cheats. Like, if it's on GitHub, you're going to get banned for using it. But that just means that there is just this availability of cheats that we don't see in a lot of other places.
cues.zh: 我觉得它很可能只需少量修改就能在 CSGO 上运行，大概花 5 到 10 分钟折腾。好消息是，我们确实能抓到几乎所有这类作弊。比如，如果它在 GitHub 上，你用就会被封禁。但这只是说明作弊的可得性很高，这在很多其他地方见不到。

cues.en: There are two main sort of cheats that are prevalent in CSGO. There's a third one that we're not really going to talk about today, but it also is just this very minor sort of issue. And the primary two are probably the two that you might be used to if you're familiar with cheating in your games. And that is basically something that helps you aim better and something that gives you information that you're not supposed to have.
cues.zh: CSGO 里主要有两类常见外挂。还有第三类，今天不打算讲，但它也只是个很次要的问题。最主要的两类，如果你熟悉游戏作弊，可能已经见过：一类帮你瞄得更准，另一类给你本不该拥有的信息。

cues.en: And you can sort of, so the aim hacks or aim bots tend to make it sort of much, much easier for you to communicate, headshot that guy. Because in CSGO, if I see a target and I want to headshot him, I need to identify him. I need to decide that he is an enemy, or she could be. Decide.
cues.zh: 自瞄外挂或瞄准机器人，会让你更容易传达“爆头那个人”这个意图。因为在 CSGO 里，我看到一个目标、想爆头时，得先识别他。我得判断他是敌人，也可能是她。得判断。

cues.en: that they're an enemy, I need to move my mouse over, I need to place it ideally on their head, push the mouse, and then start dragging it down to sort of deal with recoil. Or I could have a cheat that does all of those things if I just press the X button, including not shooting if that person is actually a friend of mine. And so that communication of intent, there's a big delta between sort of the intent of the action and the actual action.
cues.zh: 判断他是敌人后，我得把鼠标移过去，尽量放到他头上，按下鼠标，然后往下拖来压枪。或者我可以用外挂，只要按 X 键就完成所有这些，甚至在那人其实是我朋友时不开枪。所以在这种意图传达中，动作意图和实际动作之间存在很大的差距。

cues.en: And information assistance hacks are exactly what you would expect while hacks, you know, substituting materials or what have you. But it's just giving you information that basically you shouldn't have. And then there's sort of this scale that we sort of think about hacks on. There's the subtle cheats where somebody is trying to basically pretend that they're a better player than they are.
cues.zh: 信息辅助外挂正是你预料的那种，比如透视外挂，你知道，替换材质之类的。它只是给你一些你根本不该拥有的信息。然后我们还会从某种尺度来看外挂：有隐蔽型作弊，使用者基本就是想假装自己比实际更强。

cues.en: And those are actually pretty hard to detect and not what we went after first. And then sort of the scale kind of ramps up in obviousness until you get to what we call rage cheats. And the purpose of a rage cheat is not subtlety. The purpose of a rage cheat is to make you pissed off that I am cheating and there is nothing you can do about it. And all I want to do for the next 40 minutes is ruin your day. And so we decided that seemed like a pretty good target to go after first.
cues.zh: 这些其实很难检测，也不是我们最先针对的。然后这个尺度在明显程度上不断上升，直到所谓“狂暴外挂”。狂暴外挂的目的不是隐蔽，而是让你因为我在作弊而气炸，却又无能为力。我接下来 40 分钟只想毁掉你的一天。所以我们决定，这似乎是个很适合先下手的目标。

cues.en: Cheating, because of the 5v5 nature in CSGO, you can sort of think about the cheating problem as it relates to an individual user. So if I'm going to play a competitive match, given that I am clean, even a low base rate of cheating, like if 2% of players are sort of cheaters and they're randomly distributed, then 2 out of 10 matches that I play are going to be dirty. And if the base rate of cheating were 7%,
cues.zh: 在 CSGO 里，由于是 5v5，你可以从单个用户的角度来想作弊问题。如果我要打一场竞技匹配，假设我自己干净，即使作弊基础率很低，比如 2% 的玩家是作弊者且随机分布，那我打的 10 场里会有 2 场是脏的。如果作弊基础率是 7%，

cues.en: half of the matches that I get into will have at least one cheater. And that is, again, assuming that I'm a clean player because there are nine other opportunities for a cheater to land. The other thing that is maybe mildly that's slightly even more irritating about that is that given that you are a clean player, you are more likely to play against a cheater than you are to have a cheater land on your team because there are only four slots for them to land on your team and five slots for them to land on the other team.
cues.zh: 我参加的一半比赛都会至少有一个作弊者。再说一次，这是假设我自己是干净玩家，因为还有九个位置可能落到作弊者。还有一点可能更让人恼火：既然你是干净玩家，你遇到对面有作弊者的概率，比作弊者排到你队的概率更高，因为排到你队只有四个位置，而排到对面有五个位置。

cues.en: So that makes it an even more irritating problem for our sort of good actor players. Now the good news is, I'm going to spend a minute here sort of in a digression. The good news is that we don't actually just randomly distribute our players.
cues.zh: 所以这让行为良好的玩家面对的问题更恼人了。好消息是，我接下来要稍微跑个题，花一分钟讲讲。好消息是，我们其实并不会随机分配玩家。

cues.en: We released the system in 2016 called trust score and this sort of mitigates the damage of cheating a fair amount. And the idea is that we sort of pay attention. We trained a model based on how you interact with CSGO and how you interact with steam. And we use that to try and predict how likely it is that you're going to go on to receive a ban of some sort. And then we basically use that trust score to match as an additional factor when we're doing matchmaking like in addition to.
cues.zh: 我们在 2016 年发布了一个叫“信任评分”的系统，这在一定程度上减轻了作弊造成的损害。思路是我们会关注一些信号。我们训练了一个模型，依据是你如何与 CSGO 互动、如何与 Steam 互动，然后用它来预测你之后收到某种封禁的可能性有多大。接着我们在匹配时基本上会把信任评分作为额外因素，也就是除了考虑以下因素：

cues.en: your skill, and what map you want to play, and other things. And that lets us put known good actors in with other known good actors more often. And so as a result, our known good actors run into cheaters way less often. And this can be more easily visualized. Imagine this is just a population of players. Don't count them. There are 50 dots here. And so we need to set them into five V5 matches.
cues.zh: 你的技术水平、你想玩哪张地图以及其他因素。这样我们就能更频繁地把已知守规矩的玩家和其他已知守规矩的玩家排在一起。结果就是，我们已知守规矩的玩家遇到作弊者的频率低得多。这个可以更直观地展示。假设这里就是一群玩家。别数了，这里有 50 个点。然后我们需要把他们分进五场 5v5 对局。

cues.en: And because it is way easier to do with PowerPoint, maybe we set our matches up like this. Right. And so now we've created five matches and let's find out how we did. So you have this sort of concept that we're going to introduce called the rainbow of trust.
cues.zh: 因为用 PowerPoint 做起来容易多了，我们也许会把对局排成这样。对吧。现在我们排出了五场对局，来看看效果如何。于是就有了我们要引入的这个概念，叫做“信任彩虹”。

cues.en: And we think that blue players are very unlikely to go on to receive bands, but red players are very likely to go on to receive bands. And you might be asking if the red players are likely to go on to receive bands, why don't you just ban them? The answer is because they haven't cheated yet. Like, we don't know for sure that they're cheaters. They are just more likely to go on to be cheating. But let's assume in this case that five of the red players are cheating. You can see that in the worst case here, like all five of these matches now have cheaters.
cues.zh: 我们认为蓝色玩家之后收到封禁的可能性很低，而红色玩家之后收到封禁的可能性很高。你可能会问，既然红色玩家很可能之后会被封禁，为什么不直接封了他们？答案是，因为他们还没作弊。我们并不确定他们就是作弊者，只是更可能之后去作弊。但假设在这个例子里，有五名红色玩家正在作弊。你可以看到，最坏情况下，这五场对局现在全都有作弊者。

cues.en: And what trust lets us do is basically say, hey, when we're trying to build matches, if we assume all of these players are sort of that any subgroup of 10 players here would form a reasonable match, we could draw our matches like this instead. And now we've created four good matches. And the players who we're most certain are not going to go on to cheat are very unlikely to run into cheaters.
cues.zh: 信任评分让我们能做的，基本上就是：在组建对局时，如果我们假设这里任意 10 名玩家组成的子集都能形成一场合理的对局，那我们就可以改成这样来划分对局。现在我们组出了四场质量不错的对局。而那些我们最确定不会去作弊的玩家，就非常不可能遇到作弊者。

cues.en: We have a bunch of data that shows that trust works really well, but I kind of prefer the anecdotal version instead, and that's that we actually launched trust about six months before we announced it. And during that time, we were gathering feedback and looking for people that sort of like had bugs, like just general feedback, right? They didn't know that we were running the experiment, but, and so what would happen is you'd see a thread pop up on like the Steam community forums where somebody would say,
cues.zh: 我们有一堆数据表明信任评分效果非常好，但我个人更喜欢轶事版，也就是我们其实在正式公布前大约六个月就上线了信任评分。那段时间，我们在收集反馈，寻找那些遇到 bug 的人，就是一般性的反馈，对吧？他们并不知道我们在做这个实验。于是会出现这种情况：Steam 社区论坛上冒出一个帖子，有人会说：

cues.en: CSGO is filled with cheaters, and then you'd see somebody else reply, and usually quite a few someone else says, who would reply and say, I don't really ever run into cheaters anymore, I don't know what you're talking about. And at this point, we had sort of been public about some of the other anti-cheat work that we were doing, and so the player base assumed that that was why they weren't seeing cheaters as often.
cues.zh: “CSGO 全是作弊者”，然后你会看到别人回复，通常还会有不少人回复说：“我现在真的很少遇到作弊者了，不知道你在说什么。”到那时，我们已经公开过一些其他的反作弊工作，所以玩家群体就以为，这就是他们不再那么常遇到作弊者的原因。

cues.en: But we would go and basically say, hey, let's go figure out what this person's trust score is. And we'd go and we'd look at the OP, and you'd be like, this dude has types of 50 accounts, and 49 of them have bans for cheating. I don't care that that guy runs into cheaters. He should run into cheaters, because he's definitely going to cheat again, but maybe he hasn't done it yet.
cues.zh: 但我们基本会去看一下这个人的信用分是多少。一查楼主，你会发现：这家伙关联了大概 50 个账号，其中 49 个都因为作弊被封了。我才不在乎这人会不会撞到作弊者。他就该撞到作弊者，因为他肯定还会再作弊，只是现在可能还没开始而已。

cues.en: So that's pretty much all I kind of wanted to say on trust. I did want to mention, though, a thing that's cool about trust is that it doesn't really reduce the rate of cheating, but it reduces the blast radius when people decide to cheat. So let's dive in and talk about a couple of the other anti-cheat things that we do.
cues.zh: 关于信用机制我大概就想讲这么多。不过我还想提一点，信用机制很酷的地方在于，它其实并不能降低作弊率，但它能缩小有人决定作弊时的波及范围。接下来我们深入聊聊我们做的其他几项反作弊工作。

cues.en: So the main, probably the main thrust of work that we do is just mitigating exploits. We just fix bugs when they come in, and that goes away. Somebody reports, hey, here's this problem. We investigate, we figure out what the problem is, and we fix it. And so one of the canonical examples for this was this speed hack.
cues.zh: 所以我们最主要的工作重心，大概就是封堵漏洞。收到漏洞报告就修 bug，问题就解决了。有人反馈说，嘿，这里有个问题。我们排查、搞清原因、然后修复。这方面的一个典型例子就是加速挂。

cues.en: It turned out that players realized, some malicious players realized that if they, this part's a little bit technical, I'm sorry, but they basically realized that if they lied to the process, they lied to CSGO about how fast their clock was running, they could convince the game client that basically it was running 10 ticks at a time. And so then the game client would faithfully be like, hey server, here's 10 movement packets.
cues.zh: 事实证明，有些恶意玩家发现——抱歉，这部分有点技术细节——他们发现只要欺骗进程、向 CSGO 虚报时钟速率，就能让游戏客户端以为自己一次跑了 10 个 tick。于是客户端就会老老实实地对服务器说：嘿服务器，给你这 10 个移动数据包。

cues.en: And that would effectively, and then the game server was like, for reasons that client authoritative feels awesome, the game server would just go, yeah, OK, looks good to me. And it would just process all 10 movement packets in sort of a single server tick. And then the result of that is that that player would just sort of appear to just teleport around the map effectively at will.
cues.zh: 而游戏服务器呢，出于“客户端权威体验极佳”的考量，就会直接表示：行，没毛病。并在单个服务器 tick 里把这 10 个移动包全部处理掉。结果就是，那个玩家看起来就像能在地图上随意瞬移一样。

cues.en: And so the fix was basically as brutally simple as you imagine it would be. It is that the server is like, I'm, you know, modulo some latency issues. I'm only going to accept one movement packet for each client per tick. And the problem just goes away. Now, this is, like I said, this is sort of our primary form of mitigating exploits.
cues.zh: 所以修复方案也是简单粗暴到超乎想象。就是服务器规定：排除一些延迟容差之外，我每个 tick 只接受每个客户端发来的一个移动包。问题就这么迎刃而解了。正如我所说，这就是我们封堵漏洞的最主要方式。

cues.en: It's always an option. It's always ongoing work. And the thing is, is that as we do that work, like bad actors continue to probe and try and find new areas, and this sort of evolutionary behavior on their part results in this treadmill of work. And we don't mind doing the treadmill of work. It's important, valuable work, but it is a treadmill that we're sort of signed up for.
cues.zh: 这始终是一种可行手段，也是一项长期持续的工作。但问题在于，我们在做这些工作的同时，作弊者也在不断试探、寻找新的突破口，这种对抗演进就导致了一场永无止境的拉锯战。我们并不介意打这种持久战，它既重要又很有价值，但这确实是一项我们必须硬着头皮跑下去的“跑步机”工作。

cues.en: The other primary form of anti-cheat that we utilize is VAC, valve anti-cheat. And VAC basically is a system of sort of client side detections, so I'm gonna pay attention to what's going on in your system, and then I'm gonna anonymize that and scrub it of anything that might be personally identifiable, and then I'm gonna hand it up to the server.
cues.zh: 我们采用的另一种主要反作弊手段是 VAC，即 Valve 反作弊系统。VAC 基本上是一套客户端检测系统，它会监测你系统里的运行情况，然后进行匿名化处理，清除任何可能识别个人身份的信息，最后上传到服务器。

cues.en: And now that VAC is only active when you're connected to VAC secured servers, and if you receive a VAC ban, it only prohibits you from playing on VAC secured servers, but that is about 98% of servers, so you're pretty locked down at that point. And then the evidentiary standard for VAC, meaning like when VAC takes an action, we're 100% certain that you had your hand in the cookie jar with a caveat.
cues.zh: 目前 VAC 只在你连接到受 VAC 保护的服务器时才会启用，如果你被 VAC 封禁，它也只禁止你进入受 VAC 保护的服务器，但这占了大约 98% 的服务器，所以基本上你就被彻底限制了。至于 VAC 的证据标准，也就是说当 VAC 采取行动时，除了一种特殊情况外，我们百分之百确定你作弊被抓了个现行。

cues.en: And the caveat is that sometimes we make mistakes, but when we make mistakes, we rectify them clearly and immediately. There's a blog post, there's a clarification that this was the thing and it was wrong and we fixed it and we're very sorry. And as a result of this, our community has very high confidence that when VAC takes action, that we are punishing cheaters.
cues.zh: 这个特殊情况就是我们有时也会犯错，但一旦犯错，我们会公开且立刻纠正。我们会发博客澄清、承认错误、修好它并深表歉意。正因如此，我们的社区非常信任 VAC，相信只要它出手，惩罚的一定是作弊者。

cues.en: which is born out. But interestingly, I know that a lot of devs actually struggle with the opposite problem. They have an anti-cheat, and their players believe that their anti-cheat really gets cheaters, but they're not actually certain that the anti-cheat isn't also punishing innocent users. We definitely don't have that problem. We're very happy about that. Okay, so...
cues.zh: 事实也确实如此。但有趣的是，我知道很多开发者面临的恰恰是相反的困扰。他们有一套反作弊系统，玩家也相信它确实能抓到作弊者，但玩家无法确定它是否也在误伤无辜。我们绝对没有这个问题，对此我们非常欣慰。好，那么……

cues.en: We don't talk about VAC very often, and the reason that we don't talk about VAC is that talking about it makes it less effective. And in particular, talking about detections just stops them from working. So, for example, if I got up on stage today and I said,
cues.zh: 我们很少公开谈论 VAC，原因在于谈论它会降低它的有效性。尤其是谈论具体的检测手段，直接就会让它们失效。比如，如果我今天走上台说：

cues.en: Hey guys, here's a detection. What we do is when somebody has a process and their process is scribbling into CSGO's memory, we go identify all of the binary parts of that process and then we go find the executable code that loaded that process from disk and then we MD5 Summit and then we send it home and we figure out if that is a malicious actor or like OBS or something instead. When I tell you that that's a thing that we do, I just lit that thing on fire. Like it doesn't work anymore or at least...
cues.zh: 嘿伙计们，这里有个检测方法：当有人启动某个进程向 CSGO 的内存里乱写时，我们会识别该进程的所有二进制组件，找到从磁盘加载该进程的可执行代码，计算其 MD5 校验和并传回服务器，以此判断它是恶意程序还是 OBS 之类的正常软件。一旦我把这套做法讲出来，我就等于亲手把它给废了。它就彻底失效了，或者至少……

cues.en: by the time this hits Twitch in three seconds, it definitely won't work anymore. The good news is that we actually have thousands of detections that are sort of various sophistication, and we write more every day. But again, every time we do this, our bad actors evolve, and the treadmill continues. All right, great. So let's get to why we think deep learning might be an effective component in our sort of anti-cheat strategy. But before we do that, let's talk a little bit about deep learning.
cues.zh: 等这视频三秒后直播推到 Twitch 上时，它肯定就彻底失效了。好消息是，我们其实有成千上万种复杂度各异的检测手段，而且每天都在编写新的。但同样，我们每做一次更新，作弊者也在进化，这种拉锯战永远在继续。好了，太棒了。接下来聊聊为什么我们认为深度学习可以成为反作弊策略中有效的一环。不过在那之前，我们先来简单聊聊深度学习。

cues.en: So if you're not really familiar with deep learning at all, or you're just familiar with the buzzwords, then I'm going to give you the 40,000 foot view. And the basic concept behind deep learning is that deep learning can help you basically just automatically build a function that maps inputs to outputs. So if you're familiar with algebra notation, you're probably familiar with y equals f of x, right? And we're just saying like y is the result of applying some f to some input x.
cues.zh: 如果你对深度学习完全不熟，或者只熟悉那些热词，那我就给你一个四万英尺的高空概览。深度学习背后的基本概念是，它能帮你自动构建一个把输入映射到输出的函数。如果你熟悉代数记号，应该知道 y = f(x)，对吧？我们就是说，y 是把某个 f 应用到某个输入 x 上的结果。

cues.en: And the cool thing about deep learning is deep learning says, if I have enough x and I have enough y, I can solve for f. And that's pretty powerful. It turns out that then you can take that f that you have just built and you can apply it to sort of never before seen x values and get actually pretty sensible y's. And if you don't use deep learning, then engineers are writing your f values. That's that treadmill of work that we were talking about.
cues.zh: 深度学习的妙处在于，它说：如果我有足够多的 x 和足够多的 y，我就能解出 f。这相当强大。结果就是，你可以把刚构建好的 f 应用到以前没见过的 x 值上，得到相当合理的 y 值。而如果不用深度学习，就是工程师在写你的 f 值。那就是我们之前说的那种无休止的工作。

cues.en: And that lets you make this trade that Valve were really excited about. That lets us basically trade data and compute for engineering time. Because at Valve, we are always, always short on engineers, but we have a lot of data and we have a lot of compute power. cues.zh: 这让你能做 Valve 非常兴奋的那种交换。它让我们基本上用数据和算力来换取工程时间。因为在 Valve，我们一直、一直缺工程师，但我们有大量数据，也有大量算力。所以如果我拿这个类比来说，也许你没跟上代数，我把它带到现实世界，也许你会想象，如果我有一堆肉块，还有一堆汉堡肉饼，而且数量足够多，

You could, if you had enough x and y, like there is a closed form solution that is sort of the best possible f that converts that x to y. But the thing is, is that you would need so much data, so, so, so much data, like,
cues.zh: 现在你可能注意到，我说我们只是在构建一个可能的、把输入映射到输出的函数。原因基本上是数据匮乏问题。如果你有足够的 x 和 y，其实存在一个闭式解，它可以说是把 x 转成 y 的最佳 f。但问题是，你需要太多太多太多数据，像，

cues.en: quintillions of examples, quintillions and quintillions of examples, even for very simple functions. So the reality is that you're not going to do that. You're going to get just one of the myriad of possible solutions. Now, deep learning is actually really good at pattern recognition. It's really good at things that you're already familiar with, like is there a cat sitting on the sofa? The answer is yes.
cues.zh: 百亿亿级的样本，百亿亿级又百亿亿级的样本，哪怕函数非常简单。所以现实是，你不会那么做。你只会得到无数种可能解中的一个。其实深度学习非常擅长模式识别。它很擅长你已经熟悉的事情，比如沙发上有没有猫？答案是：有。

cues.en: And also, if you have a computer, the computer in your pocket, if you have interacted with Siri or Google assistance, deep learning is made use of to transform the words that you say into text that then translates to commands that then is used to sort of do fuzzy lookups. And it's used in so many pieces along the way. Now, deep learning basically operates in two modes. There's sort of training time where you're like, hey, I've got a bunch of cubes of meat and I have hamburger patties and I want to build a meat grinder.
cues.zh: 而且，如果你有电脑——也就是口袋里的手机，或者你用过 Siri、Google Assistant，深度学习就会用来把你说的话转成文本，再转成指令，进而做模糊查找。这整个链条里很多环节都用到了它。基本上，深度学习有两种运行模式。一种是训练阶段，就好像说：“我有一堆肉块，我想要汉堡肉饼，所以我要造一台绞肉机。”

cues.en: And then once you've built that meat grinder, it's like, great. Now I want to take these cubes of chicken and I want to turn those into a chicken burger, because that sounds like a thing that might be good. Deep learning that works in these two modes that we call, like I said, training and imprinting. Now I might, during the talk, accidentally say machine learning, because we actually do a fair amount of machine learning at Valve as well. And the simplest way to talk about this
cues.zh: 绞肉机造好之后就变成：“太好了，现在我想把这些鸡肉块做成鸡肉汉堡，因为听起来应该挺不错。”深度学习就是在这两种模式下工作的，正如我刚才说的，训练和推理。在接下来的演讲中，我也许会不小心说成机器学习，因为我们在 Valve 确实也做了大量的机器学习。而最简单的理解方式是——

Spoiler alert, the solution to get them to work was to have a million times as much data and a billion times as much compute. And then they work great. All right, so let's get back to our elevator pitch. So basically, we were looking at how do we attack this cheating problem. We tossed around a ton of ideas. But I really didn't want to sign up for the treadmill.

cues.en: And so looking at this, it was like, well, you know, humans, when they watch matches, they can tell that cheating is occurring. And I think that's probably because they're detecting a pattern of cheating. And deep learning is really good at detecting patterns. So like, shouldn't deep learning be able to detect cheating? And as I mentioned before, aim bots seem like both the largest, the biggest problem because
cues.zh: 所以当时仔细一想：你看，人类在观战时，其实能看出谁在开挂。我觉得这大概是因为他们识别出了作弊的行为模式。而深度学习又极其擅长模式识别。那按理说，深度学习不也能检测作弊吗？正如我之前提到的，自瞄外挂似乎是最大、最严重的问题，因为……

So it seemed like, well, we should go after those first, because if we can't do those, then we're definitely not gonna be able to do the things that are more subtle. Now, if you recall, I mentioned that deep learning is trying to solve y equals f of x for f. The problem was, like, if only we had a source for x and y. Good news, it turns out we had a source of x and y.
cues.zh: 因为它们并不隐蔽，至少很多都不怎么隐蔽。而且它们的特征信号非常强烈，至少看起来是这样。所以当时觉得，我们应该先拿它开刀；因为要是连自瞄都搞不定，更隐蔽的作弊手段我们就更不可能搞定了。还记得前面我说过，深度学习其实就是在 y = f(x) 中求解 f 吗？当时的问题是：要是我们能有 x 和 y 的数据源就好了。好消息是，事实证明我们还真有。

cues.en: For years, CSGO has had this system called Overwatch, no relation, which is a jury review system. But basically, what we have is we have players, they watch cases, and those are our X values, and then they decide guilt through some process that I don't know, I don't know what their process is, and then they render a verdict.
cues.zh: 多年来，CSGO 一直有个叫 Overwatch 的系统，跟那个游戏没关系，是一个陪审团审核系统。但基本上，我们有玩家，他们观看案件，这些就是我们的 X 值，然后他们通过某个我不知道的流程来判定是否有罪，我不知道他们的流程是什么，然后他们给出裁决。

cues.en: And they do this in this way where they go through this process. Players report other players, and then sort of central coordinator selects cases. By the way, that is a computer, it is not a person. There isn't like a guy at Valve that is like, I am the coordinator. That would be kind of cool, but it's not a thing.
cues.zh: 他们的做法是走这样一个流程。玩家举报其他玩家，然后某种中央协调器来挑选案件。顺便说一句，那是台计算机，不是人。Valve 并没有某个人说“我就是协调器”。那倒挺酷，但没这回事。

cues.en: And then the players adjudicate those cases. Other players basically decide, is this person guilty? And they do that through a process where they're sort of presented with an evidentiary window. The evidentiary window is eight rounds long, and they're asked like, hey, watch, and the play time isn't minimized, so you don't know who the players are. You watch basically a demo of eight rounds, and then at the end you're asked,
cues.zh: 然后由玩家来裁决这些案件。其他玩家基本上决定：这个人有罪吗？他们的做法是，会给他们一个证据窗口。证据窗口长八个回合，然后问他们：嘿，看一下。游戏时间没有被最小化，所以你不知道这些玩家是谁。你基本上看八个回合的录像，最后会被问到：

And we ask that for aim assistance, movement assistance, information assistance, and other assistance that we're not sure about, and also griefing. And if you're guilty, you get a bam. cues.zh: 这个人用了瞄准辅助吗？只有当你认为证据确凿、排除合理怀疑时，才判他有罪。我们会针对瞄准辅助、移动辅助、信息辅助，以及我们不太确定的其他辅助，还有恶意破坏来问这个问题。如果有罪，你就会吃封禁。如果无罪，就没有惩罚，对吧？所以它的运作方式基本符合你的预期。Overwatch 用朴素贝叶斯来寻找有罪阈值。

cues.en: That's a bunch of math-y stuff I'm not really going to go through. But the point is that, according, we have a model. Usually, convictions and overwatch, the jurors are super, super convinced that that person is a cheater.
cues.zh: 那是一堆数学的东西，我不打算细讲。但重点是，我们有一个模型。基本上，证据标准是：由你的同行判定，你有 99.8% 的可能性在作弊。而实际被定罪的比例通常是五个九。通常，在 Overwatch 的定罪中，陪审员非常非常确信那个人在作弊。
